gen-gf-warnes-gf-nata-sans: Expressive and loud, Warnes stretches out in wide, spacious letters. Its tapering ink strokes make a statement, while Nata Sans just gets on with the reading, its tall central band and open curves doing the quiet work.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-nobile: Nobile reads as a tidy sans-serif with capitals barely taller than its lowercase and curves left open like unjoined chalk arcs. Warnes is the showpiece here, bold and uniform; Nobile does the talking.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-nokora: Nokora lays down a dense, dark stripe of lowercase in every line, its s never pinching shut. Warnes is for making a loud entrance, and Nokora for carrying on after it.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Bold, stretched and a bit theatrical, Warnes keeps every stem and arc locked in step. And Noto Kufi Arabic follows as a plain sans, with a welcoming gap in its c and capitals only just above the lowercase.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans: Loud, stretched and pipe-cleaner slim at the joins. Warnes is built to make a statement, whereas Noto Sans, a plain sans with generous lowercase bodies, is built to be read.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Warnes brings a bold, stretched look with ink strokes that taper away. Noto Sans Adlam, a plain sans with tall, full curves and well-separated endings, keeps a longer text moving smoothly without crowding the eye.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-adlam-unjoine: Every stroke in Warnes is cut to one width, like laser-cut sheet. Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined gives longer text generous space between curve ends and stems, so lines move along with little height fuss between cases.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-hie: Warnes is expressive and bold, with every stroke cut to a single width and spacing stretched wide. And Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs, a modern sans-serif with outward-pointing terminals, takes over where the display letters step back.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Noto Sans Arabic reads as a plain sans with wide openings on small letters and a pronounced x-height. Yet Warnes does its best work as a bold, bowl-smooth headline, while the body font handles the steady text.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Noto Sans Armenian is approachable, with tall, full lowercase and inviting round openings. Warnes is best at bold, stretched display lines with unswelling bowls; this plain sans is best at everything after them.
